output.brief:
The Android drop is almost certainly not caused by release 6.14. It comes from a new vendor rule (AUTO-LIB-17) in Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update. The rule blocks Android password requests because their user-agent is 'nettle-http', the networking library every Android version uses. The first 403 appeared at 10:41 UTC, three minutes after the pack went live. It hit every app version within one minute, including 6.12 and 6.13, which make up about 90% of attempts. Only 5% of attempts were on 6.14. The drop doesn't vary with OS version or security-patch status. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. About 41,000 blocked installs were real customers, and 92% had logged in successfully in the prior 90 days. So this is not credential stuffing.

What to do next: ask Corvane to set AUTO-LIB-17 to log-only on the password-login path, leaving rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then check that Android password success returns to about 96%. Do not roll back 6.14 or raise bot-protection sensitivity, because either would add friction without fixing the cause. Do not exclude blocked attempts from the KPI, because that would hide the real customer impact. Longer term, require testing of vendor rule updates before they go live. My confidence is high. The one gap is that I haven't seen Corvane's own confirmation.
